title: Generics Fundamentals
ques: Explain the motivation behind **Generics** in TypeScript. Write a generic identity function `getFirstElement<T>` that accepts an array of type `T` and returns the first element of type `T | undefined`.
explanation: Generics provide reusable, flexible components that work across multiple data types while preserving exact type relationships and compile-time safety, avoiding the pitfalls of `any`.

title: Applying Generic Constraints
ques: Explain how to constrain generic type variables using the **`extends`** keyword. Write a function `logLength<T extends { length: number }>` that only accepts arguments containing a `.length` property.
explanation: Generic constraints (`T extends Type`) restrict allowed types to only those that satisfy a specific contract, allowing the function body to safely access expected properties.

title: Working with Union and Intersection Types
ques: Contrast **Union types (`|`)** and **Intersection types (`&`)**. Write a TypeScript code sample declaring both a union type for loading states and an intersection type combining two interfaces.
explanation: Union types (`A | B`) require a value to match at least one of the constituent types. Intersection types (`A & B`) require the resulting object to contain all properties from every intersected type.

title: String and Numeric Literal Types
ques: Demonstrate the use of **Literal Types** combined with unions to implement a type-safe direction controller.
explanation: Literal types allow variables to accept only specific exact strings, numbers, or booleans rather than any arbitrary primitive value.

title: Type Narrowing via typeof and instanceof
ques: Explain the concept of **Type Narrowing**. Write a function `processInput` that demonstrates narrowing using both the **`typeof`** operator and the **`instanceof`** operator.
explanation: Type narrowing uses runtime control flow guards (`typeof`, `instanceof`, `in`) to refine broad types into specific narrow types within conditional branches.

title: Implementing Discriminated Unions
ques: Explain what a **Discriminated Union** (tagged union) is. Write an exhaustive shape-calculating function `calculateArea` that handles `Circle`, `Square`, and `Rectangle` using a switch on their common literal discriminant `kind`.
explanation: A discriminated union consists of multiple object types sharing a common literal property (the discriminator). The compiler checks this tag to narrow down to the exact subtype with 100% type safety.
